verdicts.review: Article 1 ties scope to a participating-state seat and retains non-conflicting national law; national exceptions are not inferred.
Articles 309–310 support contribution-limited SARL responsibility and one or multiple natural/legal founders; guarantees remain outside scope.
Article 385 supports a single SA shareholder and contribution-limited debt responsibility.
AUDCG 44–48 separates natural-person registration from legal-person incorporation; no unsupported sole-trader liability shortcut is retained.
Complete Mali law article 2, visually checked, freely fixes total capital and separately requires equal nominal shares of at least CFA 5,000; no false total floor.
AUSCGIE 311 expressly permits contrary national provisions; the default does not override the identified Mali law.
Article 311-1 requires total subscription, full in-kind payment, at least half cash at subscription and balance within two years from RCCM registration; all conditions appear.
Article 312 uses a strict greater-than CFA 5m test for an individual or aggregate in-kind amount; special benefits independently require valuation control.
Articles 387–388 support CFA 10m ordinary SA minimum and full capital subscription before signing.

Article 389 first paragraphs support quarter cash and three years, but continuation on PDF p.96 imposes nominative-share, capital-increase and bond restrictions omitted from the condensed payment rule. Repair F1.
Articles 823–824 support CFA 100m only for the stated listing/public-placement scope; no universal private-SA figure inferred.
Article 376 visually checked: two out of three strict closing tests, assets >125m, annual turnover >250m, permanent staff >50.
Article 376 cessation depends on the two exercises before auditor mandate expiry, not one small year; candidate preserves that qualification.
Article 376 permits optional appointment below trigger and a court request by holder(s) of at least one tenth.
Articles 694–696 establish SA audit and conditional professional-register qualification; candidate does not invent a Maltese or foreign permission.
Articles 10–13 support authenticity subject to national exceptions and mandatory articles content; no current national exception assumed.
Article 313 supports immediate deposit in permitted institution/notary, receipt and articles mention.
Article 314 supports funds unavailable until registration with a court-authorised refund mechanism; candidate refers to that mechanism rather than claiming immediate refund eligibility.
Articles 137–142 support annual financial statements and management report, distinct from tax forms.
Articles 140,348,548 support six-month approval/meeting and relevant judicial extension; not confused with tax filing.
Article 269 spans PDF pp.65–66 and supports one-month financial-statement deposit plus refusal-decision branch.
Articles 98,100–101 distinguish constitution by signing/adoption and legal personality at registration, subject to Act exceptions.
AUDCG 44 and 46 support first activity month versus month of constitution for the appropriate applicant.
AUDCG 39 and 44–47 support the prescribed form and listed supporting documents; exact current form/authentication is held.
AUDCG 45 and 47 use 75 days after registration; two-month administrative wording is identified as a conflict, not substituted.
Complete government individual-enterprise procedure describes API guichet, validation, deposit acknowledgement and payment receipt; candidate limits the checklist scope.
Government page says documents vary and uses two months; candidate explicitly declines to certify an identical current company checklist.
Dated DGI NIF guidance supports register, tenancy/domiciliation, articles as relevant and card collection at tax centre/API; identifiers kept distinct.
NIF guidance month-of-start sentence is not used to override LPF112 ten-day VAT existence declaration.
Articles 101,315–316,380 support pre-registration third-party status and separate constitution/auditor defects; no unverified fine amount supplied.
AUDCG60 prevents failure to register being used to evade attached responsibilities/obligations; no invented criminal sanction.
AUSCGIE3 allows persons of any nationality to choose a permitted form; AUDCG48 separate foreign establishment registration is correctly scoped.
CGI wage, property, investment and business headings/provisions establish separate categories; routing does not aggregate them into ITS.
CGI82–84 distinguish individual/partner assessments and company IS, including elections.
BCEAO introductory history explicitly lists Mali and monetary-union CFA designation; no exchange-rate claim adopted.
CGI4 has category-specific residence/work/payer conditions and CGI44 Mali-business profits subject to ratified conventions; blanket worldwide claim is removed.
CGI5–7 wages,49 net profit,85–86 turnover minimum and198–206 VAT consideration/tax points support distinct bases; linked figure homes retain their conditions.
CGI70–79 regime distinctions and LPF23–28,57,110–115 support classification before assigning duties; no universal return model invented.
Dated DGI NIF guidance actually requests articles/register evidence; NIF application does not prove incorporation or completion of tax returns.
AUSCGIE98–101 support distinction between constitution, registration and legal personality.
LPF282 expressly excludes increases from credit for instalments paid; duplicate reconciliation is identified as a workpaper control.
CGI48 calendar year has first-period exceptions; LPF return/payment branches differ, so universal March date is properly rejected.
LPF23–28 prescribed model, signature, annexes, competent service and deposit certificate are distinct from LPF281 payment evidence and325–326 receipts.
LPF36–39,65–67,98,119–122,283–285,328,419–421 separate nonfiling, understatement, withholding and payment sanctions; overview adopts no blanket percentage.
CGI4,44,80–81,94–98,196–197 and LPF57-A support separate cross-border workstreams; no treaty rate or universal foreign exemption inferred.
Enacted finance-law46 refers to 2026 Annex U; retrieved reference does not supply annex contents or prove continuity.
CGI81(1) covers foreign dependency/control and common-group control, with outward profit transfers by prices, undercapitalisation or other means incorporated into results.
CGI81(2)(a) uses majority direct/interposed capital OR factual decision power; no false absolute ownership safe harbour.
CGI81(2)(b) extends to common control under the same tests.
CGI81(3) removes dependency/control condition for privileged/noncooperative counterparties; candidate preserves this exception.
Privileged regime is no tax OR rate lower by more than ten percentage points, not ten percent or an inclusive boundary.
Minister periodically establishes noncooperative list; current actual list is explicitly unproved.
Fallback to one specified organisation list where ministerial list absent is textually supported; candidate supplies no guessed country list.
LPF57-A I requires Mali legal person, turnover >=3bn and stated foreign dependency/control, for previous exercise; threshold does not exempt substantive TP.
LPF57-A I expressly imposes 1% declared turnover per month late, maximum5%; example assumes complete months without inventing fractions.
CGI49 supports effective costs and sufficient proof, with ordinary deductibility remaining a separate condition.
CGI51(2) addresses real/non-abnormal/non-excessive enumerated foreign charges; no unrestricted all-cost deduction inferred.
Embedded decree7 with2017 amendment labels enumerates royalties, technical assistance and affiliated purchases/sales and requires real non-excessive amounts.
Decree8 full-competition independent comparison supports case stipulated comparability; candidate rejects invented mandatory method hierarchy.
LPF57-A II(1) group information includes activity, links, functions/risks, relevant intangibles and policy.
LPF57-A II(2)(a–b) includes local activity changes and nature/amount of associated flows including royalties.
LPF57-A II(2)(c) requires cost-sharing list and copies of relevant APAs/rulings affecting results.
LPF57-A II(2)(d) method selection/application plus functions/assets/risks is preserved.
LPF57-A II(2)(e) comparables analysis is conditional on method requiring it, not unconditional mandatory database search.
LPF57-A I expressly says package substitutes for neither transaction proof nor ordinary article57 declaration.
LPF57-A III noncooperative associated branch adds beneficiary documents including balance sheet/P&L under article60.
LPF57-A I links previous-exercise simplified declaration/documentation to article57 deadline; operative/current dates remain held.
LPF57-A I administration model exists; candidate does not invent boxes/upload route.
LPF57-A IV transition concerns2016 only, not extension for current job.
LPF57-B audit request requires gathered transfer indicators, precise nature/country/entity and relevant sums; candidate preserves audit scope.
LPF57-B response at least one month and reasoned extension total<=three months is correctly distinguished.
LPF57-B insufficient response is followed by formal notice with missing answers, sanctions and one-month completion period.
LPF57-C I absent response or missing/partial documentation allows affected bases assessed from available evidence.
LPF57-C II absent precise elements permits normally operated similar-enterprise comparison; no automatic chosen mark-up supplied.
LPF57-E actual APA mechanism exists; source six-month silence/five-exercise effect are deliberately outside current method and explicitly held.
CGI44 Mali profits subject to duly ratified double-tax conventions; no current treaty entitlement supplied.
LPF61 source/use without fixed establishment is expressly subject to440; candidate does not equate domestic terms to treaty PE.
CGI94 without permanent professional installation is subject to applicable double-tax convention; scope not solely foreign bank account.
CGI94(b) rights/equipment/knowhow and services provided OR used in Mali are correctly separated.
CGI94(c) includes public contracts whatever object; candidate does not silently narrow to services.
CGI95 applies to individuals/companies of any form and visiting artists under specified conditions.
LPF440 no-NIF service branch has its own payer/service and wage-collection/sanction rules; not collapsed into441.
CGI96 service gross receipts reduced50% before rate, with separate performance prior tax reduction; ordinary figure home maintained.
CGI96 performances/concerts deduct admission duties/taxes first; case excludes this branch.
CGI96 works/contracts/supplies use90% expense deduction, not interchangeable service base.
CGI97 rate30% applies to96 base; case repeats figure-home inputs only for execution.
CGI98 says source income withholding independent from turnover-tax withholding116; candidate correctly keeps VAT separate.
CGI196 territory/use rules include immovable/event exceptions; VAT figure home used for details.
CGI196 requires proof that location outside Mali applies or deems it Mali; no blanket foreign exemption.
CGI197 accredited Mali representative first, customer payment fallback; candidate does not call all foreign purchases one reverse charge.
CGI80 applies to authorised Mali activity without headquarters and caps head-office share20% general expenses; case denominator expressly stipulated.
CGI80 defines secretariat, headquarters personnel and other parent costs for subsidiaries/establishments.
CGI49 actual/evidenced costs: cap cannot create a deduction; examples use supported amount and avoid double count.
CGI51(2) foreign charges real/non-abnormal/non-excessive; related-party evidence remains separate.
LPF616 disguising realisation/transfer cannot bind administration, which restores true character; no universal PE definition inferred.
LPF616 enumerates offshore contract components used Mali; candidate retains contract context and substance.
LPF616 distinguishes group member without stable fiscal establishment and member established with Mali NIF; NIF not treated as residence proof.
LPF57 requires global-profit declaration plus Mali activity declaration for Mali/other-state operations; no claim global income necessarily taxed.
LPF61 non-headquartered enterprise annexes consolidated balance sheet and detailed general expenses; current form held.
LPF441 source withholding previous month remits in first15 following month or next working day; not borrowed for no-NIF branch.
LPF442 unwithheld/insufficient amount attracts equal fine additional to tax; no unexplained netting.
LPF443 non-payment wording measures double sums withheld but undeclared; precise odd wording retained rather than expanded.
LPF444 refers turnover-tax interest mechanism and450; interaction/current cumulative sanctions explicitly held, no invented percentage.
